name: The Grain Lords
about: The harvest fails, and one rich house's barns are full. It sells its grain at a ransom while another lord's towns starve. Buy at its price, fix the price by decree, or seize the barns, and face either a hunger march or the hoarder's sellswords.
title: The Grain Lords

beats.speaker: hungry
beats.text: Rain rots the harvest in the fields. In {market} a loaf costs a day's wage, then two. In {barns}, {hoarder}'s granaries are full to the rafters and the doors are locked.

court.text: {hungry} of {hungry.house}: "My people eat bark, Your Grace, and {hoarder} sells grain at ten times its price to whoever has silver. I have none left."

options.label: Buy {hoarder}'s grain at his price (350 gold)
options.result: The crown pays {hoarder}'s price. Carts of grain roll to {market}, and {hoarder} buys a second fleet of barges.

options.label: Fix the price of bread by royal decree
options.result: Criers read the King's price in every market. {hoarder} reads it, and smiles.

options.label: Open the royal granaries (250 gold)
options.result: The royal granaries at Kingsmere open. They feed {market} for a season, and then they are empty.

beats.speaker: hoarder
beats.text: {hoarder} has learned what the crown will pay. The next barges from {barns} come with a new price, and a note: the King's custom is valued.

court.text: {hungry}: "He doubled it, Your Grace. He'll double it again. Every coin you pay him is a coin he spends on swords."

options.label: Pay again (450 gold)
options.hint: {market} eats · {hoarder} is the richest lord in the realm
options.result: The crown pays. {hoarder}'s steward weighs the gold twice.

options.label: Enough: fix the price by decree
options.result: The King fixes the price. {hoarder} closes {barns}' gates.

beats.speaker: hoarder
beats.text: Rather than sell at the King's price, {hoarder} burns a barn of wheat in {barns}' square, and lets the smoke drift toward {market}.

court.text: {hungry}, shaking: "He burns bread while children die, Your Grace. Take his barns, or I will."

options.label: Seize {hoarder}'s barns by royal writ
options.result: Royal men break the locks at {barns}. The grain goes to {market} under guard; {hoarder} watches from {hoarder.his} tower.

options.label: Fine {hoarder} and let it lie
options.result: {hoarder} pays the fine in full and on time, which tells everyone how little it hurt.

options.label: Withdraw the decree
options.result: The King's price is quietly forgotten. In {market}, so is the King.

beats.speaker: hungry
beats.text: The bakers' shops of {market} are stripped to the ovens. A mob drags a grain factor out of his house and hangs him from the market cross with a loaf in his mouth.

court.text: {hungry}: "I can't hold {market}, Your Grace. They want bread or they want blood, and they no longer care whose."

options.label: Feed them from the treasury (400 gold)
options.hint: the riots end · the crown is poorer
options.result: Bread carts roll into {market} under the King's banner. The mob cheers the banner, and eats.

options.label: Hang the ringleaders
options.result: Twelve hang beside the grain factor. {market} is quiet, and hungrier.

options.label: Tell the mob where {hoarder}'s barns are
options.result: A royal herald reads out the road to {barns}. The mob is on it before he finishes.

beats.speaker: hungry
beats.text: A lean winter. Nobody in {market} is fat, but nobody is buried for want of bread. Everyone watches the sky for the spring rains.

beats.speaker: hungry
beats.text: Ten thousand starving walk out of {market} behind {hungry}'s banner, toward Kingsmere and the royal granaries, singing hymns, carrying scythes.

beats.speaker: hoarder
beats.text: {hoarder} spends a famine's profits on two companies of sellswords and marches on Kingsmere, promising bread to every town that opens its gates.

beats.speaker: hungry
beats.text: The spring rains come, and then the sun. By midsummer bread in {market} costs a penny again, and the people remember which lords fed them.

beats.speaker: hungry
beats.text: {hoarder}'s sellswords are paid off and gone home. The barns of {barns} are thrown open to the realm, and the grain inside feeds three towns through the spring.
